title: Chromatic index of the prism over a graph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $K_2$ denote the complete graph on two vertices, and form the Cartesian product $G \square K_2$ — the prism over $G$, whose vertices are the pairs $(v,i)$ with $v$ a vertex of $G$ and $i \in \{0,1\}$, and in which $(v,i)$ is adjacent to $(v',i')$ exactly when either $v = v'$ and $i \neq i'$, or $i = i'$ and $v,v'$ are adjacent in $G$. Then the edge chromatic number of $G \square K_2$ — that is, the chromatic number of its line graph — equals its maximum degree $\Delta(G \square K_2)$.
replaced:
Ex 6.2.6(a)

\textbf{6.2.6} The \emph{product} of simple graphs $G$ and $H$ is the simple graph $G
\times H$ with vertex set $V(G) \times V(H)$, in which $(u, v)$ is adjacent to $(u',
v')$ if and only if either $u = u'$ and $vv' \in E(H)$ or $v = v'$ and $uu' \in E(G)$.
(a) Using Vizing's theorem (6.2), show that $\chi'(G \times K_2) = \Delta(G \times
K_2)$.
